title: runtime: per-TP-group forward-progress watchdog (quarantine + controlled teardown)
author: Samir Qureshi
description:
Context: We have recurring TP hangs/timeouts under sustained load (esp streaming + high concurrency) where a TP group stops making forward progress but continues to receive work. This PR implements a per-TP-group forward-progress watchdog in the runtime scheduler. When a group is detected as stuck, we quarantine it (stop scheduling new work to it) and initiate a controlled teardown of the worker group to avoid long-tail stuck capacity. The watchdog emits explicit metrics + structured logs for triage and alerting.

Design summary: Each TP group maintains a lightweight 'progress fingerprint' that is updated when any rank reports token-step progress (decode step), collective completion, or request completion. A watchdog task runs at a fixed cadence and evaluates (a) wall-clock time since last progress, (b) whether the group has inflight work, and (c) whether the group is already draining/quarantined. If stuck past threshold for N consecutive ticks, the group transitions to QUARANTINED, the scheduler stops admitting new requests to the group, inflight requests are failed fast with a specific error code (TP_GROUP_STUCK) to allow retry/fallback routing, and we begin a controlled teardown: signal worker threads to stop accepting work, attempt to abort collectives, and mark the group for recreation by the pool manager.

Key behavior: (1) Quarantine is TP-group scoped (failure domain = group, not host). (2) Watchdog is gated behind a feature flag default-off for this PR (enablement + thresholds are finalized in PR-18473). (3) We avoid false positives by requiring inflight > 0 and consecutive violations, and by ignoring groups currently in explicit DRAINING due to scale-down.

Changes in this PR: - Add TpGroupWatchdog component owned by SchedulerRuntime; runs periodic checks and drives state transitions. - Extend TpGroupStateMachine with QUARANTINED and TEARING_DOWN substates + hooks used by scheduler admission. - Add 'controlled teardown' path: cancel outstanding work, attempt cooperative shutdown, and hand control to TpGroupManager for group recreation. - Add metrics: runtime_tp_watchdog_triggers_total{reason}, runtime_tp_group_quarantined_total{reason}, runtime_tp_group_teardown_total{result}, runtime_tp_group_quarantined_inflight_gauge, runtime_tp_watchdog_last_progress_seconds histogram. - Add structured log event 'tp_watchdog_triggered' with group_id, model_id, pool, reason, inflight counts, last_progress_ms, and recent collective summary.

Test plan: - Unit tests for state machine transitions: HEALTHY -> QUARANTINED -> TEARING_DOWN -> (REMOVED/RECREATED). - Deterministic-ish scheduler test that simulates 'no progress' by freezing the progress counter while keeping inflight non-zero; asserts no new admission + teardown invoked once threshold met. - Integration test in runtime test harness to ensure request cancellation propagated and callers receive TP_GROUP_STUCK within bounded time.

Rollout: This lands behind Runtime flag runtime.tp.watchdog.enabled=false by default. SRE can enable on canary pools once metrics/dashboards land (observability-pack/pr-502) and thresholds are set (PR-18473). Target: Hosted canary first, then Dedicated opt-in.

Notes/limitations: This does not itself improve NCCL async error surfacing; it prevents stuck groups from consuming capacity indefinitely. If teardown fails to abort collectives on certain driver/NCCL combos, we still quarantine and rely on group recreation/host recycle policy (follow-up tracked in ENG-2406).

Refs: ENG-2407, ENG-2402; related PRs: PR-18432 (scheduler respects quarantined groups), PR-18455 (collective async error checks), PR-18470 (structured stall logs).

scheduler/tp: state machine transitions for QUARANTINED + TEARING_DOWN

conversation: Sofia Ivanova (review): Can we ensure quarantine stops admission immediately even if a batch is being formed? I’m worried about a race where we enqueue after QUARANTINED is set.

Samir Qureshi (author): Good call. I added an atomic state read in AdmitRequest() and a second check right before enqueue; also added a regression test that flips to QUARANTINED during batch formation and asserts we reject.
Hiro Tanaka (review): Teardown path calls AbortCollectives()—is this safe on all streams? We’ve seen cross-stream deadlocks when abort is called while an event is pending.

Samir Qureshi (author): In this PR we only attempt cooperative abort (no forced cudaDeviceReset). AbortCollectives() is best-effort and time-bounded; if it times out, we mark teardown_result=abort_timeout and rely on group recreation/host policy. I added a guard to avoid abort while holding scheduler locks and moved the abort call onto the TP group's control thread.
Sean Gallagher (review): Metrics naming/labels: please avoid high-cardinality labels. Do we include model_id? That would blow up Prometheus.
Samir Qureshi (author): Agree. Metrics do NOT include model_id. Structured logs include model_id for debugging. Metrics labels are limited to {pool, reason, result} with bounded enums.
Rafael Mendes (review): What’s the default threshold? Also please ensure this doesn’t page before dashboards exist.

Samir Qureshi (author): Default remains disabled. Threshold constants are placeholders (30s, 3 consecutive ticks) behind the flag; final thresholds + per-mode defaults come in PR-18473. Paging will be wired only after observability-pack/pr-502 lands.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Structured event fields: please include last_progress_ms and inflight_decode/inflight_prefill so we can split ‘stuck decode’ vs ‘stuck prefill’.
Samir Qureshi (author): Added inflight_decode / inflight_prefill counters and last_progress_ms; also included recent_collective_kind if available.
Sofia Ivanova (review): One more: When quarantining, we should fail fast but return a retriable error that router can catch.
Samir Qureshi (author): Updated error mapping to TP_GROUP_STUCK with retriable=true. Router already treats it as retryable for fallback policies; added test coverage.
release_notes: - Reliability: Adds per-tensor-parallel-group forward-progress watchdog to quarantine and tear down stuck TP groups (feature-flagged; disabled by default pending rollout).
final_outcome: Merged to main; will be enabled via staged canary once thresholds + dashboards are in place.
